title: Safe publication: ensuring other threads see a fully-constructed object, not a partial one
keyPoints: Without safe publication, another thread may see a reference to a half-constructed object with null or default fields.
The JVM or CPU may reorder instructions, publishing the reference before the constructor finishes.
Safe publication via final fields: the JMM guarantees all final fields are visible when the constructor completes.
Safe publication via volatile reference: a volatile write after construction establishes a happens-before relationship.
Safe publication via synchronized block or thread-safe collection (ConcurrentHashMap.put) provides built-in happens-before.
Double-checked locking for singletons requires a volatile field to prevent seeing a partially constructed instance.

s1_definition.oneliner: Safe publication ensures that other threads see a fully constructed object, not a partially initialized one with null fields, by using final fields, volatile references, or synchronized blocks.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Unsafe publication** – without proper synchronization, the JVM or CPU may reorder instructions so that a reference to a new object is visible to other threads before the constructor finishes. The reading thread sees non-null reference but null fields.
- **Final fields guarantee** – the JMM guarantees that all `final` fields are fully initialized and visible to any thread that obtains a reference to the object after the constructor completes (the freeze semantic).
- **Volatile reference** – writing the object reference to a `volatile` field after construction establishes a happens-before relationship. The reading thread sees the fully constructed object.
- **Synchronized/thread-safe collection** – publishing inside a `synchronized` block or via `ConcurrentHashMap.put()` provides built-in happens-before guarantees.
- **Double-checked locking** – the singleton pattern `if (instance == null) synchronized { if (instance == null) instance = new Singleton(); }` requires `volatile` on the instance field to prevent seeing a partially constructed singleton.
s1_definition.analogy: Building a new bank branch (constructing an object): unsafe publication is putting up the "NOW OPEN" sign before the vault is installed and tellers are hired. Customers walk in and find an empty building. Safe publication is finishing everything first, then putting up the sign. Final fields are like the vault being permanently installed during construction: it cannot be seen half-built. volatile is the sign on a special board that guarantees everyone sees the complete branch.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Unsafe Publication (instruction reordering):

  Thread-1 (writer)           Thread-2 (reader)
  ─────────────────           ─────────────────
  1. allocate memory
  2. assign reference ────▶   reads reference (non-null!)
  3. run constructor          reads fields (NULL! constructor not done!)

  Safe Publication (volatile):

  Thread-1 (writer)           Thread-2 (reader)
  ─────────────────           ─────────────────
  1. allocate memory
  2. run constructor
  3. volatile write ──────▶   volatile read
     (memory barrier)         (sees fully constructed object)
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Safe publication ensures that other threads see a fully constructed object, not a partially initialized one with null fields. Without it, the JVM or CPU may reorder instructions so that the reference is published before the constructor finishes. The reading thread sees non-null but finds null fields.

Four safe publication techniques: final fields (JMM freeze guarantee), volatile reference (happens-before on write), synchronized block (monitor exit happens-before), and thread-safe collections (built-in happens-before). Java records are ideal because all fields are implicitly final. Double-checked locking for singletons requires volatile to prevent the partially constructed instance bug.

Remember one sentence: publish object references only after full construction, using final fields, volatile references, or synchronized blocks to establish happens-before relationships.
